guide.headline: Cowboys lean on Lamb and third-and-long magic
guide.hook: Dallas has a top-1-percent receiver and a third-and-long offense that just does not fail, while Tampa Bay's defense has a real shot to break that streak.

items.title: CeeDee Lamb commands the field
items.what: Lamb has 37 catches for 498 yards and four touchdowns this season on a 31 percent target share, putting him in the top 1 percent of NFL wide receivers. He is playing 81 percent of offensive snaps and holds a 44 percent air yards share, so the ball finds him whether it is a quick game or a shot play.
items.when: Any third down or red zone snap when Dallas needs a chain-mover.

items.title: Cowboys own third-and-long
items.what: Dallas throws on 16 of 17 third-and-long snaps this season, a 94 percent rate, and converts 53 percent of them, best in the league at No. 1 of 31. Tampa Bay's defense allows just a 21 percent conversion rate there, No. 7 of 30 on 24 plays, so something has to give.

items.title: Buccaneers thrive when they should not
items.what: Tampa Bay ranks 25th of 32 in passing-downs success at 31 percent, but Dallas ranks dead last, 32nd of 32, allowing 55 percent on those same downs. That is a 23 percentile point gap, and it means long down-and-distance is not the trap it should be for the Buccaneers.

guide.cardLine: Dallas converts third-and-long better than anyone in football, and CeeDee Lamb is the reason why.
